cards.explanation: The answer is all the nations. Jesus says, "All the nations will be gathered before Him…" (Matthew 25:32). Not one group, not one city, ALL of them. That's a bigger crowd than my bakery on free cookie day, and I've never even had a free cookie day.

The answer is kingdom. The King says, "Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you…" (Matthew 25:34). Notice the word inherit. An inheritance is handed to you, like a warm batch of cookies somebody else baked.

The answer is False. The King says the kingdom was "…prepared for you from the foundation of the world." (Matthew 25:34). Nothing rushed about it. I'd have been sweating over that timer, but this was ready from the very start.

The answer is that they took Him in. The King says, "…I was a stranger and you took Me in…" (Matthew 25:35). Taking someone in means making room for them. I used to do that for every newcomer who slid into the junk drawer I lived in, and it felt good every time.

The answer is True. The King says, "…I was in prison and you visited Me." (Matthew 25:36). It's the last thing on His list, after hungry, thirsty, stranger, naked and sick. Showing up counts, friends.

The answer is that they keep asking when they ever saw Him that way. They ask, "Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You…" (Matthew 25:37), and then they keep going down the list through the stranger, the naked and the sick and in prison (Matthew 25:38-39). I think they're honestly stunned. It's like me asking where I put my mustache wax when it's on my face EVERY time.

The answer is that they did it for Him. The King replies, "Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me." (Matthew 25:40). What they did for them, He counts as done for Him. That answers their question right there.

The answer is the devil and his angels. The King says the eternal fire was "…prepared for the devil and his angels." (Matthew 25:41). He names exactly who it was prepared for. It's heavy stuff, friends, so I'll say it plain and leave it there.

The answer is False. The King says, "I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, I was naked and you did not clothe Me, I was sick and in prison and you did not look after Me." (Matthew 25:43). It's what they didn't do, not cruel acts. This part is heavy, friends, and I think it's worth slowing down for.

The answer is True! They say, "Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?" (Matthew 25:44). It's the same kind of question the righteous asked (Matthew 25:37-39). I think both groups were surprised, friends.

The answer is that they did not do it for Him. The King answers, "Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me." (Matthew 25:45). It mirrors what He told the righteous (Matthew 25:40). Same King, same standard.
The answer is into eternal life. Jesus ends with "…but the righteous into eternal life." (Matthew 25:46). That's where the story lands for them. It's a good ending to a heavy passage, friends.
